_what_this_is: the discover step's proposals (model call); the confirm step looks each up in the registries

proposals.title: Climate Change 2022: Mitigation of Climate Change — Chapter 12: Cross-Sectoral Perspectives (Carbon Dioxide Removal)
proposals.why: IPCC AR6 WGIII definitive assessment: CDR is a necessary element to achieve net-zero CO2 and GHG emissions globally and nationally.

proposals.title: Climate Change 2023: Synthesis Report (AR6 SYR)
proposals.why: Integrates all AR6 findings; states CDR is necessary for net-negative CO2 and to counterbalance hard-to-abate residual emissions.

proposals.title: Global Warming of 1.5°C — Special Report (SR15)
proposals.why: Foundational IPCC report establishing that all 1.5°C pathways require CDR of 100–1000 GtCO2 over the 21st century.

proposals.title: The State of Carbon Dioxide Removal — 2nd Edition
proposals.why: Most recent global independent scientific assessment of CDR progress, gaps, voluntary markets, and MRV, updated June 2024.

proposals.title: The State of Carbon Dioxide Removal — 1st Edition
proposals.why: First comprehensive global assessment of CDR status; establishes current CDR at ~2 GtCO2/yr versus multi-gigaton need.

proposals.title: Negative Emissions Technologies and Reliable Sequestration: A Research Agenda
proposals.first_author: National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine
proposals.why: US National Academies consensus report assessing benefits, risks, and sustainable scale potential of all major NETs.

proposals.title: Greenhouse Gas Removal
proposals.first_author: Royal Society and Royal Academy of Engineering
proposals.why: Joint UK academies report assessing GGR technologies and their combined deployment to meet net-zero by 2050.

proposals.title: Negative emissions—Part 1: Research landscape and synthesis
proposals.why: Landmark three-part systematic review of the entire NETs literature; clarifies role, ethics, and scale-up challenges of CDR.
